quizzes.title: Iran-U.S. Nuclear Diplomacy: Background
quizzes.passage: Nuclear diplomacy between Iran and the United States has moved through several phases. For a long period, Iran faced extensive sanctions, and its nuclear programme was the central point of dispute between the two countries. A later arrangement was reached with a group of major world powers, and it set specific terms for Iran's nuclear activities. In 2018, the United States withdrew from the nuclear agreement, and Iran then gradually scaled back its compliance with several of the commitments it had accepted. The present phase of diplomacy began in June 2026, when the United States and Iran signed the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding. The booklet describes this document as an interim diplomatic framework rather than a permanent peace treaty. The memorandum outlines a fourteen-point roadmap. It covers de-escalation of hostilities, restoration of commercial navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, discussions on sanctions relief and confidence-building measures between both countries. A proposal also envisages a comprehensive agreement backed by the UN Security Council once negotiations conclude. Phased sanctions relief and easing of restrictions on Iranian oil exports are part of the arrangement under discussion. The document also provides for oversight of implementation and for restricted assets to be unlocked. Iran has reaffirmed its nuclear pledge, and talks are to begin after key steps are taken.

questions.q: In which year was the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action concluded?
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA) to 2015.

questions.q: The JCPOA was concluded between Iran and which group of countries?
questions.explanation: The booklet states the JCPOA was concluded between Iran and the P5+1 countries.

questions.q: Under the JCPOA, Iran agreed to reduce what?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists reduction of nuclear stockpiles among Iran's JCPOA commitments.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Iran agreed to permit enhanced international inspections under the JCPOA.
Reason (R): Iran gradually scaled back compliance with several JCPOA commitments.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are in the booklet, but the scaling back of compliance does not explain why Iran accepted inspections.

questions.q: Iran's scaled-back compliance with JCPOA commitments related mainly to which two areas?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the scaled-back commitments related mainly to uranium enrichment and nuclear monitoring.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Iran agreed to restrict uranium enrichment activities under the JCPOA.
II. The JCPOA was concluded in 2013.
III. Iran agreed to reduce its nuclear stockpiles under the JCPOA.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while the JCPOA's conclusion year is 2015, not 2013.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Iran agreed to permit enhanced international inspections under the JCPOA.
II. The JCPOA was concluded between Iran and the P5 countries only.
III. Iran agreed to restrict uranium enrichment activities under the JCPOA.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II is wrong because the JCPOA was with the P5+1 countries.

quizzes.title: Iran-U.S. Accord and Its Aftermath
quizzes.passage: Iran and the United States have been locked in a long dispute over Iran's nuclear programme. For years the country lived under extensive sanctions, which shaped its economy and its relations with the wider world. A later accord was struck between Iran and a set of major world powers. That accord placed binding limits on the programme and tied those limits to changes in the wider sanctions regime. In 2018, the United States left the agreement. Iran responded by reducing its adherence to several of the commitments it had made. The Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, signed in June 2026, is an interim diplomatic framework rather than a permanent peace treaty. Its fourteen points cover an immediate end to hostilities, restoration of commercial navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, and discussions on sanctions relief. The memorandum also includes oversight of implementation, the release of frozen funds and a proposal for a comprehensive agreement backed by the UN Security Council once negotiations conclude. Iran has reaffirmed its nuclear pledge under the document, which also includes a commitment to refrain from nuclear weapon development. Phased sanctions relief and easing of restrictions on Iranian oil exports are also part of the arrangement under discussion.

questions.q: In which year was the agreement between Iran and the major powers concluded?
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the JCPOA to 2015.

questions.q: Iran's 2015 agreement was concluded with which group of countries? Give the short form.
questions.explanation: The booklet says the JCPOA was concluded between Iran and the P5+1 countries.

questions.q: Under the JCPOA, Iran agreed to restrict which activity?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists restriction of uranium enrichment activities as a key JCPOA provision.

questions.q: Under the JCPOA, what did Iran agree to reduce?
questions.explanation: The booklet says Iran agreed to reduce its nuclear stockpiles under the JCPOA.

questions.q: Under the JCPOA, which kind of inspections did Iran agree to permit?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists permission of enhanced international inspections as a JCPOA provision.

questions.q: Iran's scaled-back JCPOA compliance related mainly to uranium enrichment and which other area?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the scaled-back commitments related mainly to uranium enrichment and nuclear monitoring.

questions.q: What is the common abbreviation of the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action?
questions.explanation: The booklet uses JCPOA as the short name for the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action.

quizzes.title: The IAEA: Context and Purpose
quizzes.passage: The International Atomic Energy Agency is a central body in discussions about nuclear energy and its uses. It was founded in 1957 and is headquartered in Vienna, Austria. One of its stated aims is to promote the peaceful use of nuclear energy, and this aim sits at the core of much of its work. The agency has become prominent in the current dispute between Iran and the United States. The Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, signed in June 2026, provides for downblending of highly enriched uranium under IAEA supervision. The booklet describes that memorandum as an interim diplomatic framework rather than a permanent peace treaty. The memorandum also covers restoration of commercial navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, discussions on sanctions relief, and confidence-building measures between both countries. Its fourteen points are meant to lead toward a comprehensive agreement, which the booklet says would be backed by the UN Security Council. Negotiations on nuclear issues, regional security and sanctions relief follow the initial steps. The memorandum also provides for restricted assets to be unlocked, for oversight of implementation, and for Iran to refrain from nuclear weapon development. The agency's supervision of nuclear material is part of the arrangement under discussion.

questions.q: The 'Atoms for Peace' speech of which US president is the origin the IAEA is said to have grown out of?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the IAEA was born out of Dwight D. Eisenhower's 'Atoms for Peace' speech.

questions.q: To which UN body was the 'Atoms for Peace' speech delivered?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the speech was delivered to the UNGA in 1953.

questions.q: The IAEA's objective includes inhibiting the use of nuclear energy for what purpose?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists inhibiting use of nuclear energy for any military purpose as an IAEA objective.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The IAEA is an intergovernmental organization.
Reason (R): The IAEA was born out of a speech given in 1953.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the 1953 speech is the origin of the agency and does not explain its intergovernmental type.

questions.explanation: The booklet links Rafael Grossi to the headship, 2005 to the Nobel Peace Prize, intergovernmental status to the type, and 1953 to the speech.

III. Rafael Grossi is the head of the IAEA.

questions.explanation: Statements I and III are in the booklet, while II is wrong because the IAEA is an intergovernmental organization.

questions.explanation: Statements II and III are correct, while I is wrong because the IAEA was founded in 1957.

quizzes.title: The IAEA and the Iran Dispute
quizzes.passage: The International Atomic Energy Agency works in the field of nuclear energy and is headquartered in Vienna, Austria. It was founded in 1957. The agency's stated purpose is to promote the peaceful use of nuclear energy. It has become visible in the current dispute between Iran and the United States. The Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, signed in June 2026, provides for downblending of highly enriched uranium under IAEA supervision. The booklet describes that memorandum as an interim diplomatic framework rather than a permanent peace treaty. Its fourteen points include an immediate end to hostilities, restoration of commercial navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, and confidence-building measures between both countries. The memorandum also envisages a comprehensive agreement backed by the Security Council once negotiations conclude. Iran has reaffirmed its nuclear pledge under the document, which also includes a commitment to refrain from nuclear weapon development. The memorandum also calls for the lifting of naval restrictions and the restoration of unrestricted commercial maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Discussions on nuclear issues, regional security and sanctions relief are part of the wider process that follows these initial steps. Restricted assets are to be unlocked under the memorandum, and oversight of implementation is part of the same document.
